newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: RISING RATES OVERSHADOW ACTIVITY ON SLOVAK BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: RISING RATES OVERSHADOW ACTIVITY ON SLOVAK BOURSE.

text.p: Slovak share were little changed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with the market overshadowed by turmoil on local money and forex markets.

Money market rates on Thursday soared to record levels of 44 percent due to a liquidity crunch resulting from the central bank's strategy to keep the market short and discourage short speculative selling of the crown.
Traders said they did not expect equity trading to increase in the coming days, arguing that investors will be waiting for the result of money market crises both in Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

"The bourse continues trading low volumes because rates on the local money market are rising to such high levels few investors are trading shares here," said Peter Krutil, chief trader at Creditanstalt's Bratislava branch.
Only 445 shares were traded on the floor of the main BSE listed market as the SAX index dipped 0.41 points to 195.45.
Overall volume, boosted mainly through direct and block deals, fell to 72,139 shares, from 1,165,068 stocks traded on Wednesday, with the turnover decreasing to 39.22 million from 264.31 million.
Steel maker VSZ slipped five crowns to close at 740 while its average price -- used for calculating the index -- eased by 1.3 percent.
Oil refiner Slovnaft and oil and gas storage company Nafta closed unchanged at 1,015 crowns, and 1,400 crowns respectively.
